gaps.concept: Thyroid follicular cells arise from pharyngeal endoderm; a pyramidal lobe is persistent thyroglossal duct tissue.
gaps.why_tested: An embryology stem asks which tissue forms follicles or identifies a projection above the isthmus.

gaps.concept: Hypothalamic TRH stimulates pituitary TSH; circulating T3 and T4 suppress both through negative feedback.
gaps.why_tested: A hormone-axis stem asks why TSH changes when circulating thyroid hormone changes.

gaps.concept: TSH activates a basolateral Gs-coupled receptor, raising cAMP to stimulate follicular growth and hormone synthesis and release.
gaps.why_tested: A signaling stem asks for the second messenger downstream of TSH.

gaps.concept: The sodium–iodide symporter takes up iodide basolaterally; pendrin transports it across the apical membrane into colloid.
gaps.why_tested: A labeled follicle diagram asks where iodide enters the cell and colloid.

gaps.concept: Follicular cells endocytose iodinated colloid; lysosomal proteolysis releases T3 and T4, while MIT and DIT are deiodinated for recycling.
gaps.why_tested: A synthesis diagram asks how stored hormone is released or iodide recovered.

gaps.concept: T3 binds an intracellular nuclear receptor that regulates gene transcription.
gaps.why_tested: A receptor-mechanism stem contrasts thyroid hormone signaling with membrane receptor signaling.

gaps.concept: Excess iodide normally causes a transient Wolff–Chaikoff effect; reduced iodide uptake permits escape and renewed synthesis.
gaps.why_tested: A time-course stem asks why hormone production resumes despite continued iodide exposure.

gaps.concept: Pendred syndrome results from biallelic SLC26A4 pendrin defects and links goiter or impaired iodide organification with sensorineural hearing loss.
gaps.why_tested: A child with hearing loss and goiter prompts identification of the defective transporter.

gaps.concept: Iodine deficiency reduces hormone synthesis; compensatory TSH stimulation causes goiter and can impair fetal neurodevelopment.
gaps.why_tested: A low-iodine dietary stem asks for the mechanism of goiter or congenital neurologic injury.

gaps.concept: Subclinical hypothyroidism has elevated TSH with normal free T4; subclinical hyperthyroidism has suppressed TSH with normal free T4 and T3.
gaps.why_tested: A laboratory interpretation stem gives an abnormal TSH with thyroid hormones still in range.

gaps.concept: T3 thyrotoxicosis produces suppressed TSH and elevated T3 despite normal free T4.
gaps.why_tested: A symptomatic patient has low TSH but normal free T4; T3 testing resolves the pattern.

gaps.concept: Low serum thyroglobulin favors exogenous thyroid hormone use; elevated thyroglobulin favors thyroiditis when radioactive iodine uptake is low.
gaps.why_tested: Two patients have thyrotoxicosis and low uptake; thyroglobulin distinguishes hormone ingestion from gland leakage.

gaps.concept: High-dose biotin can falsely lower measured TSH and falsely elevate measured free T4 or T3 in susceptible immunoassays.
gaps.why_tested: An asymptomatic supplement user has laboratory results resembling hyperthyroidism.

gaps.concept: THRB-related thyroid hormone resistance causes high free T4 or T3 with nonsuppressed TSH, resembling a TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma.
gaps.why_tested: A high-thyroid-hormone, nonsuppressed-TSH stem asks for a receptor defect versus pituitary secretion.

gaps.concept: A hyperfunctioning ‘hot’ thyroid nodule is rarely malignant; a nonfunctioning ‘cold’ nodule warrants malignancy assessment.
gaps.why_tested: A radionuclide scan asks how focal uptake changes cancer suspicion.

gaps.concept: Suspicious thyroid ultrasound findings include microcalcifications, marked hypoechogenicity, irregular margins, and taller-than-wide shape.
gaps.why_tested: A nodule-imaging stem asks which lesion is most concerning for malignancy.

gaps.concept: Ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration provides cytology for a suspicious thyroid nodule.
gaps.why_tested: A nodule-investigation stem asks which test samples a sonographically suspicious lesion.

gaps.concept: Serum thyroglobulin tracks differentiated follicular-cell thyroid cancer after thyroid removal; calcitonin is a marker of medullary C-cell cancer.
gaps.why_tested: A postoperative marker stem asks which thyroid-cell product corresponds to the tumor lineage.

gaps.concept: Lithium inhibits thyroid hormone release; amiodarone can disrupt thyroid function and inhibit peripheral T4-to-T3 conversion.
gaps.why_tested: A medication-exposure stem asks why thyroid hormone levels or TSH changed.

gaps.concept: Methimazole and propylthiouracil can cause agranulocytosis; propylthiouracil has greater severe liver-injury risk, and methimazole can cause embryopathy.
gaps.why_tested: A thionamide-treated patient develops fever, liver injury, or a characteristic fetal defect.
